research.thaumaturgicbrewing.base.title: Thaumaturgic Brewing
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.base.stage_: Brewing is an interesting art. It doesn't appear to utilize thaumaturgy, but the results it produces are undeniably special. I suspect that, with some effort, I could recreate its effects more efficiently using alchemical principles.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.basic_potio: By studying some of the more basic products of brewing, I should be able to learn how to recreate them using essentia.
Success! I've devised several recipes for creating potions with alchemy, using Alkimia essentia as a binder. Now to see how I can expand on that.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.advanced_po: I've been unable so far to recreate some of the more complex brewing recipes using a water base. Perhaps augmenting existing potions will get me the results I'm after...
My theory was correct. By using an existing potion as a catalyst, I'm now able to create more complex types of potions.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.harmful_pot: Like thaumaturgy, brewing has a dark side. Is it worth recreating that as well?
As I suspected, a simple inversion of effect using Perditio essentia was enough to turn helpful potions into debilitating ones. Not that I'd recommend actually drinking any of them.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.strong_basi: Brewing allows for several types of potions to be given an enhanced effect with the addition of redstone dust. Perhaps that amplification process can be reproduced alchemically as well.
A splash of Potentia did the trick. That shouldn't surprise me, given how chock full of the stuff redstone is, but I confess that I'd expected it to be a bit more... complicated.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.strong_adva: I wonder if advanced potions can have their effects amplified in the same way that basic potions can. This warrants further experimentation.
Just like basic potions, a touch of Potentia was enough to make my advanced potions more powerful.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.strong_harm: Can my debilitating potions be made more powerful? Is it worth the cost?
For better or worse, these foul concoctions are even more potent than before.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.long_basic_: Several types of brewed potions can have the duration of their effects extended by adding some glowstone dust to the mix. How do I recreate that with alchemy?

Strangely enough, Lux essentia was the answer. I wouldn't have expected it to have time-related effects, but then again it is found in the glowstone that brewing uses. Perhaps there's some unseen connection between the two arts.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.long_advanc: It stands to reason that if basic potions can have their effects extended, then advanced potions should as well. Only one way to find out.
As with my earlier experiments, a little bit of Lux has extended the effects of my advanced potions.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.long_harmfu: Perhaps these debilitating potions can have their effects extended as well. Assuming, of course, that I'm willing to partake in that kind of research.
Light is a strange thing to be adding to such dark mixtures, but alchemy doesn't always conform to our expectations. Nonetheless, it accomplished my goals here.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.splash_poti: Sometimes I don't want to drink a potion myself, but rather apply its effects to another. At a brewing stand I'd add a pinch of gunpowder to cause the flask to burst. How can I recreate that effect using essentia?
The gunpowder angle was a red herring, but I've found my answer. By adding some Aqua essentia to the any potion, I can cause it to splash readily upon contact with a surface.
research.thaumaturgicbrewing.lingering_p: Some rare brews can have their effects linger in a cloud upon exposure to the air, but the main ingredient for that, dragon's breath, isn't the easiest thing to come by. I'm going to need another solution if I want to replicate this.
A little outside-the-box thinking has brought to me the answer: Spiritus! Just as the spirits of the lost linger, so too shall any potions that I infuse with it.
